Script.name: Elemental Bond Manager
Script.script:
-- ===================================================================== -- Templar Elemental Bond Manager -- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Tracks the four elemental bonds (air/water/fire/earth), their current -- strength / load / drain, your recorded per-element maximums, your live -- active buffs (parsed from `templar_command list all`), and the measured -- channel efficiency so the auto-balancer knows how lossy channeling is. -- -- Nothing here sends a command on its own except when you invoke an alias. -- =====================================================================
bond = bond or {}
bond.elements = { "air", "water", "fire", "earth" }
-- Element label colors, matched to the game's own `list elements` output: -- air = cyan, water = blue, fire = red, earth = yellow (dim ANSI palette). -- "combined" buffs aren't an element row; show them in white. bond.elemColor = { air = "cyan", water = "blue", fire = "red", earth = "yellow", combined = "white", } function bond.col(e) return bond.elemColor[(e or ""):lower()] or "white" end
-- Current readings from `list elements`: bond.cur.fire = {strength, load, drain} bond.cur = bond.cur or {}
-- Recorded maximums (captured manually via `setmax`). bond.max = bond.max or {}
-- Active buffs, keyed by lowercased spell name. -- bond.buffs["armourplate on direkein"] = { name=<original case>, element="combined", expires=<os.time>, dur="11m 16s" } bond.buffs = bond.buffs or {}
-- Measured channel efficiency (flow / requested). Learned from the -- "resulting in a flow of N units" line. Seeded with a sane default. bond.eff = bond.eff or 0.68
-- Spells we never want auto-ended. bond.protected = bond.protected or { ["shield of faith"] = true }
-- guild command prefix bond.cmd = "templar_command"
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -- small helpers -- --------------------------------------------------------------------- local function trim(s) return (s:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "")) end
function bond.have_all_max() for _, e in ipairs(bond.elements) do if not bond.max[e] then return false end end return true end
-- ===================================================================== -- 1. READING THE ELEMENTS TABLE -- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Lines look like: FIRE : 1618 : 38 : -2 : -- Trigger pattern (PCRE): ^(AIR|WATER|FIRE|EARTH)\s*:\s*(\d+)\s*:\s*(\d+)\s*:\s*([+-]?\d+) -- which calls bond.readElementLine(matches[2], matches[3], matches[4], matches[5]) -- ===================================================================== function bond.readElementLine(elem, strength, load, drain) local e = elem:lower() bond.cur[e] = { strength = tonumber(strength), load = tonumber(load), drain = tonumber(drain), } if bond.quiet then deleteLine() end end
-- ===================================================================== -- 2. CAPTURING MAXIMUMS (alias: setmax) -- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -- We can't just read "strength at zero load" because buffs are usually up. -- Instead we reconstruct the unloaded ceiling from what's on screen: -- true_max ~= current_strength + load (load is the per-tick pull) -- but the cleaner signal the game gives is the `resulting drain` column, -- which already nets flow minus load. The most robust capture is simply: -- take the current strength and ADD BACK the load, since with no buffs the -- bond settles at strength where drain hits 0. We store the highest we see. -- -- Because you only run this judiciously (ideally with buffs down, or with a -- known buff set), `setmax` records exactly what's on screen as the ceiling. -- ===================================================================== function bond.setMax() if not next(bond.cur) then cecho("\n<red>[bond]<reset> No element data yet. Run 'tcle' first, then 'setmax'.\n") return end
-- The displayed strength already IS the ceiling; load is a separate -- per-tick figure, not a deduction from it. The reliable capture moment is -- when load is 0 (all buffs down), where strength == true max. If load is -- non-zero we still record the displayed strength but flag it as a floor, -- because active buffs can suppress the displayed value below the real max. local anyLoaded = false for _, e in ipairs(bond.elements) do local c = bond.cur[e] if c and (c.load or 0) > 0 then anyLoaded = true end end
if anyLoaded then cecho("\n<yellow>[bond]<reset> Note: some bonds show load > 0 (buffs active).\n") cecho("<yellow>[bond]<reset> For a clean max, run 'endbuffs', wait for load to hit 0, then 'setmax'.\n") cecho("<yellow>[bond]<reset> Recording current strengths anyway (treat as a lower bound):\n") else cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Recording zero-load bond strengths as maximums:\n") end
for _, e in ipairs(bond.elements) do local c = bond.cur[e] if c then bond.max[e] = c.strength cecho(string.format(" <yellow>%-5s<reset> max = <green>%d<reset>%s\n", e:upper(), c.strength, (c.load or 0) > 0 and string.format(" <grey>(load %d \226\137\160 0)<reset>", c.load) or "")) end end cecho("<cyan>[bond]<reset> Maximums stored. The balancer will aim for these.\n") end
-- ===================================================================== -- 3. CHANNEL EFFICIENCY LEARNING -- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Line: You channel 150 units of fire energy into earth, resulting in a flow of 106 units. -- Pattern: ^You channel (\d+) units of \w+ energy into \w+, resulting in a flow of (\d+) units -- ===================================================================== function bond.learnEff(requested, flow) requested, flow = tonumber(requested), tonumber(flow) if requested and requested > 0 and flow then local r = flow / requested -- light smoothing so one odd reading doesn't dominate bond.eff = (bond.eff * 0.5) + (r * 0.5) end end
-- ===================================================================== -- 4. MANUAL CHANNEL SHORTCUT (alias: chan <n> <from> <to>) -- ===================================================================== local elemAlias = { a="air", air="air", w="water", wat="water", water="water", f="fire", fire="fire", e="earth", ear="earth", earth="earth", } function bond.resolveElem(x) if not x then return nil end return elemAlias[x:lower()] end
-- Channeling adjacency: a bond cannot channel to itself or to its elemental -- counterpart. The counterparts (opposites) are fire<->water and earth<->air. -- So the only BLOCKED pairs are {fire,water} and {earth,air}; every other -- pair is a legal direct channel. bond.opposite = { fire = "water", water = "fire", earth = "air", air = "earth", }
function bond.canChannel(from, to) if from == to then return false end if bond.opposite[from] == to then return false end return true end
-- For a blocked (counterpart) pair, find a legal intermediate bond that is -- adjacent to BOTH from and to. e.g. fire->water can go via air or earth. -- Returns the intermediate element name, or nil if none (shouldn't happen -- with 4 elements, but guarded). function bond.intermediateFor(from, to) for _, mid in ipairs(bond.elements) do if mid ~= from and mid ~= to and bond.canChannel(from, mid) and bond.canChannel(mid, to) then return mid end end return nil end
-- Append channel step(s) to a plan to move energy from `from` to `to`, given -- a desired DELIVERED flow at the destination. Returns the donor cost (units -- the source loses). Handles the counterpart case by routing through an -- intermediate, where efficiency applies twice. -- plan entries: { n = requested_units, from = e, to = e, flow = delivered } -- For a two-hop, two entries are appended and the second is tagged via=mid. function bond.emitChannel(plan, from, to, deliveredFlow, eff) if deliveredFlow < 1 then return 0 end if bond.canChannel(from, to) then local requested = math.floor(deliveredFlow / eff) if requested < 1 then return 0 end local flow = math.floor(requested * eff) plan[#plan+1] = { n = requested, from = from, to = to, flow = flow } return requested -- donor loses 'requested' end -- counterpart: route via intermediate, efficiency twice local mid = bond.intermediateFor(from, to) if not mid then return 0 end -- to deliver 'deliveredFlow' at 'to', the mid must send deliveredFlow/eff, -- and 'from' must send (deliveredFlow/eff)/eff. local midSend = math.floor(deliveredFlow / eff) -- units leaving mid local fromSend = math.floor(midSend / eff) -- units leaving from if fromSend < 1 or midSend < 1 then return 0 end local arriveMid = math.floor(fromSend * eff) -- units arriving at mid local arriveTo = math.floor(arriveMid * eff) -- units arriving at to plan[#plan+1] = { n = fromSend, from = from, to = mid, flow = arriveMid } plan[#plan+1] = { n = arriveMid, from = mid, to = to, flow = arriveTo, via = true } return fromSend -- donor (from) loses 'fromSend' end
function bond.channel(n, from, to) from, to = bond.resolveElem(from), bond.resolveElem(to) n = tonumber(n) if not (n and from and to) then cecho("\n<red>[bond]<reset> Usage: chan <amount> <from> <to> (e.g. chan 100 fire earth)\n") return end if from == to then cecho("\n<red>[bond]<reset> Source and target element are the same.\n") return end if bond.canChannel(from, to) then send(bond.cmd .. " channel " .. n .. " " .. from .. " to " .. to) return end -- Blocked counterpart pair: route through an intermediate (two hops). The -- flow is multiplied by efficiency TWICE, so we tell the user what to expect. local mid = bond.intermediateFor(from, to) if not mid then cecho("\n<red>[bond]<reset> " .. from .. " cannot channel to " .. to .. " (counterparts) and no route was found.\n") return end local eff = (bond.eff and bond.eff > 0.05) and bond.eff or 0.68 local arriving = math.floor(n * eff * eff) cecho(string.format("\n<yellow>[bond]<reset> %s and %s are counterparts (no direct channel). " .. "Routing via <yellow>%s<reset>: %d \226\134\146 %s \226\134\146 %s (~%d arriving after two hops).\n", from, to, mid, n, mid, to, arriving)) send(bond.cmd .. " channel " .. n .. " " .. from .. " to " .. mid) tempTimer(0.4, function() send(bond.cmd .. " channel " .. n .. " " .. mid .. " to " .. to) end) end
-- ===================================================================== -- 4b. CHANGE SHORTCUT (alias: chg <spell> <element>) -- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Only 'element barrier' and 'tool of elemental justice' are changeable. -- 'chg barrier earth' -> templar_command change element barrier to earth -- 'chg tool air' -> templar_command change tool of elemental justice to air -- We also optimistically update the tracked buff's element locally so the -- 'bonds' display reflects the change immediately (the game's confirmation -- line "draw upon the power of X" doesn't say which spell changed, so we -- trust the spell we just targeted). -- ===================================================================== local changeable = { barrier = { full = "element barrier", keys = { "element barrier" } }, tool = { full = "tool of elemental justice", keys = { "tool of elemental justice" } }, -- a couple of forgiving aliases b = { full = "element barrier", keys = { "element barrier" } }, t = { full = "tool of elemental justice", keys = { "tool of elemental justice" } }, }
function bond.change(which, elem) local spec = which and changeable[which:lower()] elem = bond.resolveElem(elem) if not (spec and elem) then cecho("\n<red>[bond]<reset> Usage: chg <barrier|tool> <element> (e.g. chg barrier earth)\n") cecho("<grey>[bond] Only 'element barrier' and 'tool of elemental justice' can be changed.<reset>\n") return end send(bond.cmd .. " change " .. spec.full .. " to " .. elem) -- optimistic local update of tracked element for _, k in ipairs(spec.keys) do if bond.buffs[k] then bond.buffs[k].element = elem end end cecho(string.format("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Changing <yellow>%s<reset> to draw from <yellow>%s<reset>.\n", spec.full, elem)) end
-- ===================================================================== -- 5. AUTO-BALANCE (alias: tcbal) -- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Goal: raise the weakest bonds toward their recorded max by channeling -- surplus out of the strongest bonds. We measure each bond's deficit -- (max - strength). Donors are bonds at/near max; receivers are the ones -- furthest below. We size each channel by the *requested* amount needed, -- grossing up for the lossy flow (requested = needed / efficiency), and we -- never pull a donor below its own max minus what it can spare. -- ===================================================================== function bond.balance(opts) opts = opts or {} local dryrun = opts.dryrun
if not bond.have_all_max() then cecho("\n<red>[bond]<reset> Maximums not set for all elements. Run 'setmax' first.\n") return end if not next(bond.cur) then cecho("\n<red>[bond]<reset> No current element data. Run 'tcle' then try again.\n") return end
-- Build deficit / surplus lists. local recv, donor = {}, {} for _, e in ipairs(bond.elements) do local c = bond.cur[e] if c then local deficit = bond.max[e] - c.strength if deficit > 20 then recv[#recv+1] = { e = e, need = deficit } elseif deficit < -5 then -- above recorded max (moon phase shifted it up): can donate the excess donor[#donor+1] = { e = e, spare = -deficit + 0 } end end end
-- If nothing is meaningfully above max, allow the strongest in-range bonds -- to act as donors down to a floor, so we can still even things out. if #donor == 0 then -- rank bonds by headroom above their own "comfortable" level (90% of max) for _, e in ipairs(bond.elements) do local c = bond.cur[e] if c then local floor = bond.max[e] * 0.90 if c.strength > floor then donor[#donor+1] = { e = e, spare = c.strength - floor } end end end end
table.sort(recv, function(a,b) return a.need > b.need end) table.sort(donor, function(a,b) return a.spare > b.spare end)
if #recv == 0 then cecho("\n<green>[bond]<reset> All bonds within ~20 of their max. Nothing to balance.\n") return end if #donor == 0 then cecho("\n<yellow>[bond]<reset> Bonds are low but no donor has spare strength. " .. "Consider ending a buff instead.\n") return end
local eff = (bond.eff and bond.eff > 0.05) and bond.eff or 0.68 local plan = {}
local di = 1 for _, r in ipairs(recv) do local needFlow = r.need while needFlow > 10 and di <= #donor do local d = donor[di] if d.spare <= 10 then di = di + 1 else -- desired delivered flow this step, limited by donor spare. For a -- direct hop the donor loses ~flow/eff; for a two-hop ~flow/eff^2. -- Cap the delivered amount so the donor's loss stays within its spare. local twoHop = not bond.canChannel(d.e, r.e) local effPow = twoHop and (eff * eff) or eff local maxDeliverable = math.floor(d.spare * effPow) local deliver = math.min(needFlow, maxDeliverable) if deliver < 5 then di = di + 1 else local cost = bond.emitChannel(plan, d.e, r.e, deliver, eff) if cost <= 0 then di = di + 1 else d.spare = d.spare - cost needFlow = needFlow - deliver end end end end end
if #plan == 0 then cecho("\n<yellow>[bond]<reset> Couldn't build a useful channel plan (amounts too small).\n") return end
cecho(string.format("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Balance plan (efficiency ~%.0f%%):\n", eff*100)) for _, p in ipairs(plan) do cecho(string.format(" channel <yellow>%d<reset> %s -> %s (~%d flow)%s\n", p.n, p.from, p.to, p.flow, p.via and " <grey>(via-hop)<reset>" or "")) end
if dryrun then cecho("<grey>[bond] dry run \226\128\148 nothing sent. Use 'bal' to execute.<reset>\n") return end
-- stagger the sends slightly so the game processes each cleanly local delay = 0 for _, p in ipairs(plan) do tempTimer(delay, function() send(bond.cmd .. " channel " .. p.n .. " " .. p.from .. " to " .. p.to) end) delay = delay + 0.4 end -- refresh the table afterwards tempTimer(delay + 0.3, function() send(bond.cmd .. " list elements") end) end
-- ===================================================================== -- 5b. TICK-CONVERGENCE BALANCE (alias: rbal) -- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Goal: make the four bonds reach their maximums at about the SAME time. -- "Time to max" for a bond = deficit / drain, where deficit = max - strength -- and drain is the per-tick gain (the 'resulting drain' column). Only bonds -- with a POSITIVE drain are actually climbing; a bond with drain <= 0 is -- bleeding and never reaches max on its own (treated as infinite ticks, so -- it has top priority to receive energy). -- -- Channeling moves strength instantly: +flow into the receiver (cuts its -- deficit, so fewer ticks to max), -requested out of the donor (raises its -- ticks). We iteratively move energy from the bond with the FEWEST ticks-to- -- max (closest to full) into the bond with the MOST, recomputing after each -- step, until the spread between max and min ticks is small or no useful -- move remains. Drain is assumed unchanged by channeling (an approximation: -- real drain shifts a little as load moves, so rbal re-reads the table at the -- end so the next 'bonds'/'rbal' uses fresh numbers). -- ===================================================================== function bond.ticksToMax(strength, mx, drain) local deficit = mx - strength if deficit <= 0 then return 0 end -- already at/above max if not drain or drain <= 0 then return math.huge end -- bleeding: never refills return deficit / drain end
function bond.rbalance(opts) opts = opts or {} local dryrun = opts.dryrun
if not bond.have_all_max() then cecho("\n<red>[bond]<reset> Maximums not set for all elements. Run 'setmax' first.\n") return end if not next(bond.cur) then cecho("\n<red>[bond]<reset> No current element data. Run 'tcle' then try again.\n") return end
local eff = (bond.eff and bond.eff > 0.05) and bond.eff or 0.68
-- Working copy of projected strengths (we simulate channels here). local st, mx, dr = {}, {}, {} for _, e in ipairs(bond.elements) do local c = bond.cur[e] if not c then cecho("\n<red>[bond]<reset> Missing data for " .. e .. ". Run 'tcle'.\n") return end st[e] = c.strength mx[e] = bond.max[e] dr[e] = c.drain or 0 end
-- Helper to compute current ticks-to-max for every element. local function allTicks() local t = {} for _, e in ipairs(bond.elements) do t[e] = bond.ticksToMax(st[e], mx[e], dr[e]) end return t end
-- Show the starting picture. cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Tick-convergence balance (equalize time-to-max):\n") do local t = allTicks() for _, e in ipairs(bond.elements) do local tv = t[e] local tstr = (tv == math.huge) and "<red>bleeding<reset>" or (tv == 0 and "<green>at max<reset>" or string.format("%.0f ticks", tv)) cecho(string.format(" <%s>%-5s<reset> %d/%d drain %+d -> %s\n", bond.col(e), e:upper(), st[e], mx[e], dr[e], tstr)) end end
-- Classify bonds. -- gaining : drain > 0 and below max -> these we equalize ticks-to-max -- bleeding : drain <= 0 and below max -> channeling can't refill them -- full : at/above max local plan = {} local MIN_FLOW = 10 local FLOOR_PCT = 0 -- no artificial floor: donors may give down to need -- (the energy-balance solve sets the real targets)
-- A bond is a "climber" whenever its drain is positive: it will refill on -- its own, so under the convergence solve it can sit BELOW max now and climb -- back by the shared target time T. Crucially this includes bonds that are -- currently AT max -- they have surplus strength to donate to slower climbers -- without falling behind. (The old test `st[e] < mx[e]` excluded at-max -- bonds, so when only one bond was below max the solver saw <2 climbers and -- refused to channel, even though the three capped bonds could each spare -- energy.) Bonds with drain <= 0 that are below max are bleeders: channeling -- tops them up but can't change their drain. local bleeders, gaining = {}, {} for _, e in ipairs(bond.elements) do if dr[e] > 0 then gaining[#gaining+1] = e elseif st[e] < mx[e] then bleeders[#bleeders+1] = e end end
-- Solve for a common time-to-max T across the gaining bonds, conserving -- energy (accounting for channel loss). For a target time T, a gaining bond -- wants strength target_e = mx_e - dr_e * T. Bonds whose target is below -- current are donors (give the surplus); above current are receivers (need -- inflow). Channel loss means receivers need MORE raw donor energy than the -- flow they gain, so the energy-balanced T satisfies: -- sum(donor surplus) == sum(receiver need) / efficiency -- We bisect T to satisfy that, then emit one net channel per donor/receiver -- pairing (greedy match) -- no reversals, no ping-pong. if #gaining >= 2 then local function netAt(T) -- returns (totalDonorSurplus, totalReceiverNeed) local give, need = 0, 0 for _, e in ipairs(gaining) do local target = mx[e] - dr[e] * T -- clamp target to [floor, max] local floor = mx[e] * FLOOR_PCT if target < floor then target = floor end if target > mx[e] then target = mx[e] end local delta = target - st[e] if delta < 0 then give = give + (-delta) else need = need + delta end end return give, need end
-- Bisect T to find the energy-balance crossing. At small T, targets sit -- near max => large receiver 'need', small donor 'give'. At large T, all -- targets hit the floor => large 'give', zero 'need'. The balanced point is -- where donor energy exactly covers the grossed-up receiver need, i.e. -- f(T) = give*eff - need crosses zero (negative at small T, positive at big T). local Tlo, Thi = 0, 0 for _, e in ipairs(gaining) do local tmax = (mx[e] - mx[e]*FLOOR_PCT) / math.max(dr[e], 0.01) if tmax > Thi then Thi = tmax end end Thi = Thi + 50 local Tbest = (Tlo + Thi) / 2 for _ = 1, 50 do Tbest = (Tlo + Thi) / 2 local give, need = netAt(Tbest) local f = give * eff - need if f > 0 then Thi = Tbest -- too generous (donors over-supply) -> lower T else Tlo = Tbest -- not enough supply -> raise T end end
-- Build donor/receiver lists at Tbest. local donors, recvs = {}, {} for _, e in ipairs(gaining) do local target = mx[e] - dr[e] * Tbest local floor = mx[e] * FLOOR_PCT if target < floor then target = floor end if target > mx[e] then target = mx[e] end local delta = target - st[e] if delta <= -MIN_FLOW then donors[#donors+1] = { e = e, give = -delta } elseif delta >= MIN_FLOW then recvs[#recvs+1] = { e = e, need = delta } end end
-- Greedy match donors to receivers (largest first). Adjacency-aware: -- counterpart pairs route through an intermediate (efficiency twice). table.sort(donors, function(a,b) return a.give > b.give end) table.sort(recvs, function(a,b) return a.need > b.need end) local di = 1 for _, r in ipairs(recvs) do local needFlow = r.need while needFlow >= MIN_FLOW and di <= #donors do local d = donors[di] if d.give < MIN_FLOW then di = di + 1 else local twoHop = not bond.canChannel(d.e, r.e) local effPow = twoHop and (eff * eff) or eff -- deliverable to receiver given donor's remaining 'give' local maxDeliver = math.floor(d.give * effPow) local deliver = math.min(needFlow, maxDeliver) if deliver < MIN_FLOW then di = di + 1 else local cost = bond.emitChannel(plan, d.e, r.e, deliver, eff) if cost <= 0 then di = di + 1 else d.give = d.give - cost needFlow = needFlow - deliver end end end end end end if #bleeders > 0 then local names = {} for _, e in ipairs(bleeders) do names[#names+1] = e:upper() end cecho(" <yellow>note:<reset> <red>" .. table.concat(names, ", ") .. "<reset> have negative drain (bleeding). Channeling tops them up but\n") cecho(" won't change the drain \226\128\148 to truly fix, end a buff or change an element.\n") end
if #plan == 0 then cecho(" <yellow>No useful channels \226\128\148 every climbing bond is already converging, or only bleeders remain (end a buff / change an element).<reset>\n") return end
cecho(string.format(" <grey>plan (efficiency ~%.0f%%):<reset>\n", eff * 100)) for _, p in ipairs(plan) do cecho(string.format(" channel <yellow>%d<reset> %s -> %s (~%d flow)%s\n", p.n, p.from, p.to, p.flow, p.via and " <grey>(via-hop)<reset>" or "")) end -- Projected result: apply the plan to a copy and report the spread of -- time-to-max across the gaining bonds (the ones rbal actually equalizes). do local proj = {} for _, e in ipairs(bond.elements) do proj[e] = st[e] end for _, p in ipairs(plan) do proj[p.from] = proj[p.from] - p.n proj[p.to] = proj[p.to] + p.flow end local lo, hi = math.huge, 0 for _, e in ipairs(bond.elements) do if dr[e] > 0 and proj[e] < mx[e] then local tk = (mx[e] - proj[e]) / dr[e] if tk < lo then lo = tk end if tk > hi then hi = tk end end end if hi > 0 and lo ~= math.huge then cecho(string.format(" <grey>projected time-to-max spread (gaining bonds): %.0f-%.0f ticks<reset>\n", lo, hi)) end end
if dryrun then cecho("<grey>[bond] dry run \226\128\148 nothing sent.<reset>\n") return end
local delay = 0 for _, p in ipairs(plan) do tempTimer(delay, function() send(bond.cmd .. " channel " .. p.n .. " " .. p.from .. " to " .. p.to) end) delay = delay + 0.4 end tempTimer(delay + 0.3, function() send(bond.cmd .. " list elements") end) end
-- ===================================================================== -- 6. BUFF TRACKING (parsed from `templar_command list all`) -- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Active-spell lines look like: -- <fire> : Tool of elemental justice on voltaic titanium blade ... <13m 20s>. -- <combined> : Shield of faith on Direkein <12m 8s>. -- These can wrap across two screen lines; the <Nm Ns> duration may be on the -- continuation line. We handle that with a multiline trigger that joins the -- spell name with whatever duration token appears. -- -- Parsing strategy: a perl trigger captures the element + the text after the -- colon on the FIRST line; a second pattern grabs the <..m ..s> duration. -- To keep it robust against wrapping we parse the *element + name* on the -- element line and capture duration separately if present on the same line. -- =====================================================================
-- Parse one full logical spell line (element, descriptive text incl duration). function bond.parseSpellLine(elem, rest) -- rest is everything after "<elem> : " -- Guard: only fire|air|water|earth|combined are real buff tags. The trigger -- already restricts this, but double-check here so a stray channel line -- (e.g. "<party>: X reports ...") can never be ingested as a buff. local validElem = { fire=true, air=true, water=true, earth=true, combined=true } if not validElem[tostring(elem):lower()] then return end -- Reject obvious channel/report chatter that shares the <tag>: shape. if rest and (rest:find("reports%s+'") or rest:find("%f[%w]HP:%f[%W]") or rest:find(">>")) then return end -- spell name = text up to " on " (weapon/player), duration = <..m ..s> rest = trim(rest) local dur = rest:match("<(%d+m?%s*%d*s?)>%.?%s*$") or rest:match("<([^>]+)>%.?%s*$") -- spell name is the leading part before " on " local name = rest:match("^(.-)%s+on%s+") or rest:gsub("%s*<[^>]*>%.?%s*$", "") name = trim(name) if name == "" then return end
-- Target: everything after " on ", with trailing <...> tokens stripped. -- For weapon spells the game accepts the quoted name (e.g. "snek"); for -- player spells it's the player name (e.g. Direkein). We prefer a quoted -- name if one exists, otherwise the cleaned "on <X>" text. local target = nil local after = rest:match("%s+on%s+(.+)$") if after then -- strip any glow / duration <...> tokens after = after:gsub("%s*<[^>]*>", ""):gsub("%.%s*$", "") after = trim(after) local quoted = after:match('named%s+(%b"")') or after:match('(%b"")') if quoted then target = quoted -- keep the quotes; game expects on "snek" else target = after -- e.g. Direkein end end
local key = name:lower() local expires = nil local remain = nil if dur then local m = tonumber(dur:match("(%d+)m")) local s = tonumber(dur:match("(%d+)s")) remain = (m or 0)*60 + (s or 0) expires = os.time() + remain end
-- Track the highest remaining-duration ever seen for this buff; that becomes -- the meter's "full" (max) so the gauge drains from full=fresh to empty= -- expiring. Recasting a buff that reads higher than before raises the max. bond.maxdur = bond.maxdur or {} if remain and remain > (bond.maxdur[key] or 0) then bond.maxdur[key] = remain end
bond.buffs[key] = { name = name, element = elem:lower(), target = target, dur = dur, expires = expires, maxdur = bond.maxdur[key], -- snapshot of the meter ceiling } if bond.quiet then deleteLine() end end
-- Called when `list all` reports nothing active. function bond.clearBuffs() bond.buffs = {} if bond.quiet then deleteLine() end end
-- Called by the "stop the flow ... into your <name>." trigger. function bond.endedSpell(name) if not name then return end name = trim(name):gsub("%.$", "") local key = name:lower() if bond.buffs[key] then bond.buffs[key] = nil else -- try a looser match (the end-message wording can differ slightly) for k in pairs(bond.buffs) do if k:find(key, 1, true) or key:find(k, 1, true) then bond.buffs[k] = nil break end end end end
-- "into all of your active spells" => everything gone. function bond.endedAll() bond.buffs = {} end
function bond.listBuffs() if bond.scrubBuffs then bond.scrubBuffs() end if not next(bond.buffs) then cecho("\n<grey>[bond]<reset> No buffs currently tracked.\n") return end cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Tracked active buffs:\n") local now = os.time() for _, b in pairs(bond.buffs) do local left = b.expires and (b.expires - now) or nil local tstr if left then local L = math.max(0, left) tstr = string.format("%dm %02ds", math.floor(L/60), L % 60) else tstr = b.dur or "?" end local prot = bond.protected[b.name:lower()] and " <green>[kept]<reset>" or "" -- Color the <element> tag to match the game. Pad to align names; the -- visible tag text is "<element>" (literal angle brackets). local tagText = "<" .. b.element .. ">" local pad = string.rep(" ", math.max(0, 9 - #tagText)) cecho(string.format(" <%s>%s<reset>%s %s <grey>(%s)<reset>%s\n", bond.col(b.element), tagText, pad, b.name, tstr, prot)) end end
-- ===================================================================== -- 7. ENDING BUFFS -- =====================================================================
-- endbuffs : end everything (uses the guild's own 'end all'). function bond.endAll() send(bond.cmd .. " end all") end
-- endbuff <partial name> : end ONE tracked buff, looking up its proper target -- so you never get "X is not currently on <player>". Matches abbreviations and -- partial names against tracked buffs (e.g. 'endbuff hard', 'endbuff ap', -- 'endbuff avatar'). If the text matches more than one buff, lists the matches. function bond.endNamed(query) if not query or query:gsub("%s", "") == "" then cecho("\n<red>[bond]<reset> Usage: endbuff <name> (e.g. endbuff hard, endbuff avatar)\n") return end local q = query:lower():gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "")
-- Gather candidates: match against full name AND abbreviation. local matches = {} for key, b in pairs(bond.buffs) do local abbr = (bond.abbrFor and bond.abbrFor(b.name) or ""):lower() if key == q or abbr == q or key:find(q, 1, true) or abbr:find(q, 1, true) then matches[#matches+1] = b end end
if #matches == 0 then cecho("\n<yellow>[bond]<reset> No tracked buff matches '" .. query .. "'.\n") cecho("<grey>[bond] run 'tcla' if your buff list may be stale, or 'bonds' to see what's tracked.<reset>\n") return end if #matches > 1 then -- prefer an exact full-name or exact abbreviation match if present local exact = nil for _, b in ipairs(matches) do local abbr = (bond.abbrFor and bond.abbrFor(b.name) or ""):lower() if b.name:lower() == q or abbr == q then exact = b break end end if exact then matches = { exact } else cecho("\n<yellow>[bond]<reset> '" .. query .. "' matches several buffs \226\128\148 be more specific:\n") for _, b in ipairs(matches) do cecho(" <yellow>" .. (bond.abbrFor and bond.abbrFor(b.name) or b.name) .. "<reset> (" .. b.name .. ")\n") end return end end
local b = matches[1] local cmd = bond.cmd .. " end " .. b.name if b.target and b.target ~= "" then cmd = cmd .. " on " .. b.target end cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Ending <yellow>" .. b.name .. "<reset>" .. (b.target and b.target ~= "" and (" on " .. b.target) or "") .. ".\n") send(cmd) -- optimistic untrack + refresh the panel bond.buffs[b.name:lower()] = nil if bond.ui and bond.ui.rebuild then pcall(bond.ui.rebuild) end end
-- keepfaith : end every tracked buff individually EXCEPT protected ones. function bond.endExceptProtected() if not next(bond.buffs) then cecho("\n<yellow>[bond]<reset> No tracked buffs. Run 'tcla' (list all) first so I know what's up.\n") return end local toEnd = {} for key, b in pairs(bond.buffs) do if not bond.protected[key] then toEnd[#toEnd+1] = b end end if #toEnd == 0 then cecho("\n<green>[bond]<reset> Nothing to end \226\128\148 only protected buffs are up.\n") return end cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Ending " .. #toEnd .. " buff(s), keeping protected ones:\n") local delay = 0 for _, b in ipairs(toEnd) do local cmd = bond.cmd .. " end " .. b.name if b.target and b.target ~= "" then cmd = cmd .. " on " .. b.target end cecho(" <grey>" .. cmd:gsub(bond.cmd, "tc") .. "<reset>\n") tempTimer(delay, function() send(cmd) end) delay = delay + 0.4 end end
-- Allow adding/removing protected spells at runtime: keepalso <name> / keepnot <name> function bond.keepAlso(name) if not name or name == "" then return end bond.protected[name:lower()] = true cecho("\n<green>[bond]<reset> Will now keep: <yellow>" .. name .. "<reset>\n") end function bond.keepNot(name) if not name or name == "" then return end bond.protected[name:lower()] = nil cecho("\n<green>[bond]<reset> No longer protecting: <yellow>" .. name .. "<reset>\n") end
-- status overview. arg "maxima" shows just the recorded ceilings. function bond.status(arg) if arg and arg:lower():match("max") then cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Recorded maximums:\n") if not next(bond.max) then cecho(" <grey>none set \226\128\148 run 'setmax' (ideally just after 'endbuffs')<reset>\n") return end for _, e in ipairs(bond.elements) do local mx = bond.max[e] cecho(string.format(" <%s>%-5s<reset> %s\n", bond.col(e), e:upper(), mx and tostring(mx) or "<grey>unset<reset>")) end return end -- Default: refresh element + spell data quietly first, then display. bond.refreshThenStatus() end
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Quiet refresh: silently query `list elements` and `list all`, gag their -- raw output, then render the clean status panel once the data is in. -- The parsing triggers check bond.quiet and delete their matched lines. -- --------------------------------------------------------------------- bond.quiet = bond.quiet or false
-- Gag the current line if a quiet refresh is in progress. Used by triggers -- that match the table header and spell-wrap continuation lines, which carry -- no data we need but would otherwise clutter the screen during 'bonds'. function bond.gagIfQuiet() if bond.quiet then deleteLine() end end
function bond.refreshThenStatus() bond.quiet = true -- send muted (second arg false suppresses the input echo in the main window) send(bond.cmd .. " list elements", false) send(bond.cmd .. " list all", false) -- Give the game a beat to reply (triggers parse + gag), then render and -- drop quiet mode. 0.3s is plenty at normal latencies. if bond._statusTimer then killTimer(bond._statusTimer) end bond._statusTimer = tempTimer(0.35, function() bond.quiet = false bond._statusTimer = nil bond.renderStatus() end) end
-- The actual rendering (no querying). Called after a quiet refresh, and can -- also be called directly if you want to show cached values. function bond.renderStatus() cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> ===== Elemental Bond Status =====\n") for _, e in ipairs(bond.elements) do local c = bond.cur[e] local mx = bond.max[e] if c then local pct = mx and string.format("%3.0f%%", c.strength/mx*100) or " ? " local mxs = mx and tostring(mx) or "unset" local dcol = (c.drain or 0) >= 0 and "green" or "red" cecho(string.format(" <%s>%-5s<reset> %5d / %-5s (%s) drain <%s>%+d<reset>\n", bond.col(e), e:upper(), c.strength, mxs, pct, dcol, c.drain or 0)) else cecho(string.format(" <%s>%-5s<reset> (no data)\n", bond.col(e), e:upper())) end end cecho(string.format(" channel efficiency ~<yellow>%.0f%%<reset>\n", (bond.eff or 0.68)*100)) bond.listBuffs() end
-- ===================================================================== -- 8. BUFF BUTTON PANEL (Geyser UI, fixed-slot grid) -- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -- A fixed panel of slots (2 rows x 6 = 12), anchored to the top of the -- right-hand chat console and spanning its width. Each active buff fills -- one slot left-to-right, top row first; empty slots are hidden. -- Left-click : end that spell (templar_command end <name> on <target>) -- Right-click : for the two changeable spells (element barrier, -- tool of elemental justice), a 4-element picker. -- Slots are created once and reused (shown/hidden), which is why the -- buttons render reliably -- the earlier Adjustable.Container hosted its -- children in a content area that left simple labels invisible. -- ===================================================================== bond.ui = bond.ui or {}
-- BUILD MIGRATION. bond.ui is a persistent global, so when this script is -- re-saved/reinstalled over a previously-loaded version, the OLD widgets -- (bond.ui.panel/container/slots) survive in the table. ensure() early-returns -- when bond.ui.panel exists, so without this the NEW code would never rebuild -- and you'd keep seeing the old layout (and a stale build trace). We stamp a -- build id; if it changed (or is missing), tear down every widget this package -- has ever created and start fresh. bond.ui.BUILD = "corner-11" -- bumped: fixed 6-col grid, no window scaling if bond.ui._build ~= bond.ui.BUILD then -- Stop any drain ticker from a prior build before dropping handles. if bond.ui.ticker then pcall(killTimer, bond.ui.ticker); bond.ui.ticker = nil end -- Hide any Geyser objects from prior versions by their known names. local stale = { "bondContainer", "bondPanel", "bondBar2" } for i = 1, 12 do stale[#stale+1] = "bondSlot_" .. i end for i = 1, 24 do stale[#stale+1] = "bondTile_" .. i end for i = 1, 24 do stale[#stale+1] = "bondSq_" .. i end for _, nm in ipairs(stale) do pcall(function() if hideWindow then hideWindow(nm) end end) end -- Also hide via live Geyser handles if we have them. if bond.ui.panel then pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:hide() end) end if bond.ui.slots then for _, s in pairs(bond.ui.slots) do pcall(function() s:hide() end) end end bond.ui.panel = nil bond.ui.container = nil bond.ui.parent = nil bond.ui.slots = nil bond.ui.diag = nil bond.ui.WIDTH = 374 -- reset on build change bond.ui._build = bond.ui.BUILD end
-- Scrub any buffs that a previous build mis-ingested from channel lines -- (e.g. "<party>: X reports ..."). Keep only entries with a real element tag. do local validElem = { fire=true, air=true, water=true, earth=true, combined=true } if type(bond) == "table" and type(bond.buffs) == "table" then for k, b in pairs(bond.buffs) do local e = b and tostring(b.element or ""):lower() if not validElem[e] then bond.buffs[k] = nil end end end end
bond.ui.ROWS = 2 bond.ui.COLS = 6 bond.ui.SLOTS = bond.ui.ROWS * bond.ui.COLS
-- ===== Buff bar width (TUNABLE) ===================================== -- The bar sits in the top-right corner (y=0 down to the momentum bar). This -- is the single knob for its width; icesus's top banner is shrunk to end -- exactly at the bar's left edge, so changing this moves BOTH. Defaults to a -- little wider than the right column (borderRight, usually 360). bond.ui.WIDTH = bond.ui.WIDTH or 374 -- Set false to disable the per-second drain animation (static colored tiles -- with a time label, repainted only on buff changes). Use this to test whether -- the periodic repaint is causing any UI sluggishness: `buffbar meters`. bond.ui.useMeters = (bond.ui.useMeters ~= false) -- ===================================================================
-- Visibility intent: "on" = always visible (even with no buffs), nil = -- automatic (show only when buffs exist), "off" = hidden until 'buffbar' run. -- Default is "on" so the styled panel is always present; `buffbar off` hides it. bond.ui.forced = bond.ui.forced or "on"
-- Short labels per spell (edit freely). Kept to ~5 chars so they fit the -- square tiles without clipping. The '^' change marker is added separately. bond.abbr = { ["armourplate"] = "AP", ["avatar of the gods"] = "Avtr", ["element barrier"] = "Barr", ["instrument of the gods"] = "Instr", ["shield of faith"] = "Faith", ["tool of elemental justice"] = "Tool", ["tool of hard justice"] = "Hard", ["tool of swift justice"] = "Swift", }
-- Hex colors per element for the slot background. bond.uiColor = { air = "#1f6f8b", -- cyan-teal water = "#27408b", -- blue fire = "#8b2020", -- red earth = "#6b6b1f", -- olive combined = "#7a6a20", -- gold }
-- Which spells can be changed, and the keyword chg expects. bond.changeKeyword = { ["element barrier"] = "barrier", ["tool of elemental justice"] = "tool", }
function bond.abbrFor(name) return bond.abbr[name:lower()] or name:sub(1, 5) end
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Geometry: the buff bar sits in the TOP-RIGHT CORNER of the client, from -- y=0 down to the top of the momentum bar (~the banner height). It is a -- top-level overlay pinned to the right edge, width = bond.ui.WIDTH. The -- icesus banner is shrunk to end at this bar's left edge (see bond.ui.fitBanner), -- so the two sit side by side instead of overlapping. -- --------------------------------------------------------------------- function bond.ui.geometry() local top = 92 pcall(function() if getBorderTop then top = getBorderTop() end end) if not top or top < 1 then top = 92 end
local W = tonumber(bond.ui.WIDTH) or 420 if W < 80 then W = 80 end
-- Bottom at the banner/right-column boundary (abs y = borderTop), which is -- just above the momentum bar (momentum starts at borderTop+6). Top at y=0. -- Pin to the right edge with the "-W" constraint; height = borderTop. return "-" .. W, 0, W, top, nil -- top-level overlay (parent=nil) end
-- Shrink (or restore) icesus's top banner so its right edge meets the buff -- bar's left edge. Driven by bond.ui.WIDTH, so tuning the bar width moves the -- banner too. Reversible via bond.ui.fitBanner(true) on teardown. function bond.ui.fitBanner(restore) local banner = icesus and icesus.hud and icesus.hud.banner if not banner then return end if restore then pcall(function() banner:resize("100%", nil) end) return end local W = tonumber(bond.ui.WIDTH) or 420 -- Leave a 1px seam so the borders don't visually merge. pcall(function() banner:resize("100%-" .. W, nil) end) end
-- Build the backdrop bar once, as a direct child of icesus.hud.right. The -- individual clickable square tiles are created on demand in rebuild() (also -- as direct children of R, styled + shown immediately -- the pattern proven -- to paint). We never nest in an intermediate container and never hide a tile -- at build time; both were the causes of the earlier invisible grid. function bond.ui.ensure() if not Geyser then return end if bond.ui.panel then return end -- already built
local x, y, w, h, parent = bond.ui.geometry()
bond.ui.diag = {} local function step(label, fn) local ok, res = pcall(fn) bond.ui.diag[#bond.ui.diag+1] = label .. ": " .. (ok and "ok" or ("ERR " .. tostring(res))) if not ok then error(label .. " -> " .. tostring(res), 0) end return res end
bond.ui.parent = parent bond.ui.baseY = tonumber(y) or 0 bond.ui.barW = tonumber(w) or 348 bond.ui.barH = tonumber(h) or 84 -- baseX must be an ABSOLUTE left-edge pixel for tile arithmetic. When x is a -- Geyser "-N" constraint (top-level pinned to the right border), convert it -- to mainWidth - N. When it's already a number (in-container), use it. local nx = tonumber(x) if type(x) == "string" and x:match("^%-%d") then local mw = 1000 pcall(function() if getMainWindowSize then mw = (getMainWindowSize()) or mw end end) bond.ui.baseX = mw - (tonumber(x:sub(2)) or 360) else bond.ui.baseX = nx or 6 end
bond.ui.panel = step("panel", function() local cons = { name = "bondBar2", x = x, y = y, width = w, height = h } if parent then return Geyser.Label:new(cons, parent) else return Geyser.Label:new(cons) end end)
step("panel-style", function() -- Match icesus.core's panel look: bgMain fill, subtle border, 3px radius, -- the same JetBrains Mono stack. (icesus palette: bgMain #131629, -- bgPanel #1a1e35, border #2a2f4e.) bond.ui.panel:setStyleSheet([[ background: #131629; color: #8b90a5; border: 1px solid #2a2f4e; border-radius: 4px; font-family: "JetBrains Mono", "DejaVu Sans Mono", "Courier New", monospace; font-size: 13pt; qproperty-alignment: 'AlignCenter'; ]]) end) pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:setFontSize(11) end) -- NOTE: we deliberately do NOT call enableClickthrough here. A top-level -- clickthrough Label was capturing/forwarding mouse events across the whole -- main console on this Mudlet build, which left the MUD window looking frozen -- with a stuck text cursor. icesus's own panels are plain solid Labels with -- no clickthrough, and they don't cause this -- so we match that: a solid -- backdrop confined to the top-right corner, with the clickable tiles layered -- on top. The backdrop only occupies its own region, so it never sits over -- the main console and can't freeze it.
-- Tile pool (created lazily in rebuild). Each is a direct child of R. bond.ui.slots = bond.ui.slots or {} bond.ui.container = parent -- compatibility shim
-- Shrink icesus's banner so it ends at this bar's left edge. Done once on -- build; bond.ui.show()/setwidth re-run it when the width changes. bond.ui.fitBanner() end
-- Create (once) or fetch a square tile Label at pool index idx. Tiles are -- DIRECT children of icesus.hud.right and are shown immediately when filled. function bond.ui.getTile(idx, sizePx) if bond.ui.slots[idx] then return bond.ui.slots[idx] end local parent = bond.ui.parent local tile local cons = { name = "bondSq_" .. idx, x = bond.ui.baseX, y = bond.ui.baseY, width = sizePx, height = sizePx, } local ok = pcall(function() if parent then tile = Geyser.Label:new(cons, parent) else tile = Geyser.Label:new(cons) end end) if not ok or not tile then return nil end bond.ui.slots[idx] = tile return tile end
-- A clickable end-buff menu, echoed to the main window when the bar is clicked. function bond.ui.clickMenu() local list = {} for _, b in pairs(bond.buffs) do list[#list + 1] = b end if #list == 0 then cecho("\n<grey>[bond]<reset> No tracked buffs to end.\n") return end table.sort(list, function(a, b) return (a.name or "") < (b.name or "") end) cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> End a buff: ") for _, b in ipairs(list) do local nm = b.name echoLink("[" .. bond.abbrFor(nm) .. "]", function() local cmd = bond.cmd .. " end " .. nm if b.target and b.target ~= "" then cmd = cmd .. " on " .. b.target end send(cmd) bond.buffs[nm:lower()] = nil bond.ui.rebuild() end, "end " .. nm, true) cecho(" ") end cecho("\n") end
-- Build a horizontal drain-fill background: solid element colour from the left -- up to `ratio`, then a dark "spent" colour for the remainder. As the buff -- expires the ratio shrinks and the colour recedes leftward (full=fresh). local function drainFill(color, ratio) ratio = math.max(0, math.min(ratio or 0, 1)) local empty = "#11141f" -- Use SOLID colours outside a safe middle band. Near 0 or 1 a -- qlineargradient with near-coincident stops can render incorrectly or, on -- some Qt builds, stall -- which lined up with the client freezing exactly -- when a meter reached 0s. Below ~3% show solid empty; above ~97% show solid -- fill; only build a gradient in between, with well-separated stops. if ratio <= 0.03 then return empty elseif ratio >= 0.97 then return color end -- Keep the two stops a clear distance apart (>= 1%) so they never coincide. local lo = ratio local hi = math.min(ratio + 0.01, 1) return string.format( "qlineargradient(x1:0, y1:0, x2:1, y2:0, " .. "stop:0 %s, stop:%.3f %s, stop:%.3f %s, stop:1 %s)", color, lo, color, hi, empty, empty) end
-- Remaining-time ratio for a buff (1=fresh, 0=expired), using the highest -- duration ever seen for that buff as the meter ceiling. local function buffRatio(b) local mx = b.maxdur or (bond.maxdur and bond.maxdur[(b.name or ""):lower()]) if not mx or mx <= 0 then return 1 end local left = (b.expires or 0) - os.time() if left < 0 then left = 0 end return left / mx end
local function fmtLeft(b) local left = (b.expires or 0) - os.time() if left < 0 then left = 0 end if left >= 60 then return string.format("%dm", math.floor(left/60)) else return string.format("%ds", left) end end
-- Render the tracked buffs as TWO ROWS of clickable duration-meter tiles. -- Left-click : end that buff (templar_command end <name> [on <target>]) -- Right-click : for changeable buffs (Barrier / Tool), a 4-element picker. -- Each tile is a horizontal meter that drains as the buff expires. function bond.ui.rebuild() if not Geyser then return end if bond.scrubBuffs then bond.scrubBuffs() end -- drop any channel-line pollution bond.ui.ensure() if not bond.ui.panel then return end -- Refresh baseX from the live window size every rebuild so tiles always -- align with bondBar2 regardless of when ensure() originally ran. do local mw = 1920 pcall(function() if getMainWindowSize then mw = getMainWindowSize() or mw end end) local W = tonumber(bond.ui.WIDTH) or 374 bond.ui.baseX = mw - W bond.ui.barW = W end
-- Honor "off": hide the bar and every tile, stop the drain timer. if bond.ui.forced == "off" then pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:hide() end) for _, t in ipairs(bond.ui.slots) do pcall(function() t:hide() end) end bond.ui.stopTicker() return end
local list = {} for _, b in pairs(bond.buffs) do list[#list + 1] = b end table.sort(list, function(a, b) return (a.name or "") < (b.name or "") end)
-- Empty: hide tiles; show the styled placeholder panel if forced "on", -- otherwise hide the bar. The placeholder matches icesus's muted panel look -- (textDim label on the bgMain fill) so an empty bar reads as an intentional -- HUD panel, not a black box. if #list == 0 then for _, t in ipairs(bond.ui.slots) do pcall(function() t:hide() end) end bond.ui.stopTicker() if bond.ui.forced == "on" then pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:show() end) pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:raise() end) bond.ui.panel:echo( [[<center><span style="color:#5b6178;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:1px">]] .. [[no active buffs</span></center>]]) else pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:hide() end) end return end
-- Show the solid backdrop as the panel background (icesus-style), then layer -- the clickable tiles on top of it. Clickthrough is no longer used, so the -- backdrop is safe -- it stays in its top-right corner region and the tiles, -- raised above it, catch their own clicks. pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:show() end) pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:lower() end) -- keep it behind the tiles pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:echo("") end) -- clear any placeholder text
-- TWO-ROW layout. Always 6 columns per row (bond.ui.COLS), fixed tile size. -- Tiles do NOT stretch to fill the bar width; the 6-slot grid is fixed so -- the layout stays consistent regardless of how many buffs are active or -- how wide the window is. local n = #list local barH = bond.ui.barH or 42 local rows = 2 local gap = 3 local perRow = bond.ui.COLS -- always 6; never scale to buff count local cellH = math.floor((barH - gap) / rows) -- row height -- Fixed tile width: enough for the label + time, regardless of bar width. local cellW = math.floor((bond.ui.WIDTH - gap * (perRow + 1)) / perRow) if cellW < 24 then cellW = 24 end if cellH < 12 then cellH = 12 end
bond.ui.tileMeta = {} -- remember per-tile data for the drain ticker
for i, b in ipairs(list) do local r = math.floor((i - 1) / perRow) -- 0-based row local c = (i - 1) % perRow -- 0-based col local tile = bond.ui.getTile(i, cellW) if tile then local elem = (b.element or "combined") local bg = bond.uiColor[elem] or "#444" local label = bond.abbrFor(b.name) local key = b.name:lower() local changeable = bond.changeKeyword[key] ~= nil local kw = bond.changeKeyword[key] local spellName, spellTarget = b.name, b.target
local x = bond.ui.baseX + c * (cellW + gap) local y = bond.ui.baseY + r * (cellH + gap) pcall(function() tile:move(x, y) end) pcall(function() tile:resize(cellW, cellH) end)
-- Paint the drain meter + label. style/echo are split so the ticker -- can cheaply re-call paintTile() without recomputing layout. bond.ui.tileMeta[i] = { buff = b, color = bg, label = label, changeable = changeable } bond.ui.paintTile(i, true)
pcall(function() tile:setToolTip(changeable and (spellName .. " (Left: end Right: change element)") or (spellName .. " (click to end)")) end) pcall(function() tile:setClickCallback(function(event) local btn = type(event) == "table" and event.button or "LeftButton" if btn == "RightButton" and kw then bond.ui.elementMenu(kw, label) else local cmd = bond.cmd .. " end " .. spellName if spellTarget and spellTarget ~= "" then cmd = cmd .. " on " .. spellTarget end send(cmd) bond.buffs[spellName:lower()] = nil bond.ui.rebuild() end end) end) pcall(function() tile:show() end) pcall(function() tile:raise() end) end end
-- Hide any leftover tiles beyond the current buff count. for i = n + 1, #bond.ui.slots do pcall(function() bond.ui.slots[i]:hide() end) end
bond.ui.startTicker() end
-- Paint one tile. To keep the UI responsive we AVOID calling setStyleSheet on -- every tick -- repeated stylesheet reparsing/relayout on many labels is what -- made the client feel frozen. We only re-issue the gradient stylesheet when -- the meter's fill BUCKET (whole-percent step) actually changes; the cheap -- text echo (time remaining) happens every tick. function bond.ui.paintTile(i, force) local meta = bond.ui.tileMeta and bond.ui.tileMeta[i] local tile = bond.ui.slots and bond.ui.slots[i] if not meta or not tile then return end local ratio = buffRatio(meta.buff) local bucket = math.floor(ratio * 100 + 0.5) -- 0..100 if force or meta.bucket ~= bucket then meta.bucket = bucket pcall(function() tile:setStyleSheet(string.format([[ background: %s; color: #eef0f6; border: 1px solid #2a2f4e; border-radius: 3px; font-weight: 700; qproperty-alignment: 'AlignCenter'; ]], drainFill(meta.color, ratio))) end) pcall(function() tile:setFontSize(8) end) end tile:echo(string.format( [[<center><span style="color:#eef0f6;font-weight:700">%s%s</span>]] .. [[<span style="color:#c8cdd8"> %s</span></center>]], meta.label, (meta.changeable and [[<span style="color:#fbbf24">^</span>]] or ""), fmtLeft(meta.buff))) end
-- Remove any buff whose element isn't a real bond element. Defends against -- channel chatter ("<party>: X reports ...") that a stale/old trigger from a -- prior install might still feed in. Cheap; safe to call often. function bond.scrubBuffs() local valid = { fire=true, air=true, water=true, earth=true, combined=true } if type(bond.buffs) ~= "table" then return end for k, b in pairs(bond.buffs) do local e = b and tostring(b.element or ""):lower() local nm = b and tostring(b.name or "") if not valid[e] or nm:find("reports") or nm:find(">>") or nm:find("HP:") then bond.buffs[k] = nil end end end
-- Drain ticker: a SINGLE repeating timer (every 2s). The 4th arg `true` makes -- tempTimer repeat on its own until killed -- so the callback must NOT create -- another timer. (A prior version both passed `true` AND re-called -- startTicker() each tick, spawning an exponentially growing pile of repeating -- timers that eventually hard-froze the whole client. That was the freeze.) function bond.ui.startTicker() if not bond.ui.useMeters then return end -- animation disabled if bond.ui.ticker then return end -- already running; never dup bond.ui.ticker = tempTimer(2, function() -- Do NOT nil the id and do NOT reschedule here -- this timer repeats itself. if bond.ui.forced == "off" or not bond.ui.tileMeta or not next(bond.ui.tileMeta) then return end -- Reap any buff whose timer has run out, then a single rebuild. local now, reaped = os.time(), false for k, b in pairs(bond.buffs) do if b.expires and (b.expires - now) <= 0 then bond.buffs[k] = nil reaped = true end end if reaped then bond.ui.rebuild() return end for i in pairs(bond.ui.tileMeta) do bond.ui.paintTile(i) end end, true) end
function bond.ui.stopTicker() if bond.ui.ticker then pcall(killTimer, bond.ui.ticker) bond.ui.ticker = nil end end
-- Right-click element picker (kept for the chg flow): clickable choices. function bond.ui.elementMenu(keyword, label) cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Change <yellow>" .. label .. "<reset> to: ") for _, e in ipairs({ "fire", "air", "water", "earth" }) do echoLink("[" .. e:upper() .. "]", function() bond.change(keyword, e); bond.ui.rebuild() end, "change " .. label .. " to " .. e, true) cecho(" ") end cecho("\n") end
-- Show / hide / re-anchor controls (buffbar alias). function bond.ui.show() bond.ui.forced = "on" local ok, err = pcall(function() bond.ui.ensure() end) if not ok then cecho("\n<red>[bond] buff panel failed to build:<reset> " .. tostring(err) .. "\n") cecho("<grey>[bond] type 'buffbar where' to see which step failed.<reset>\n") return end pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:show() end) pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:raise() end) if bond.ui.fitBanner then bond.ui.fitBanner() end if next(bond.buffs) then bond.ui.rebuild() end send("templar_command list all") end
-- Toggle the drain animation on/off (diagnostic + preference). function bond.ui.toggleMeters() bond.ui.useMeters = not bond.ui.useMeters if not bond.ui.useMeters then bond.ui.stopTicker() end bond.ui.rebuild() cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Drain animation " .. (bond.ui.useMeters and "<green>ON<reset>" or "<yellow>OFF<reset>") .. ".\n") end
-- Set the bar width (and re-fit the banner). Usage: buffbar width 460 function bond.ui.setWidth(n) local w = tonumber(n) if not w or w < 80 then cecho("\n<yellow>[bond]<reset> Usage: buffbar width <pixels> (e.g. buffbar width 460)\n") cecho("<grey>[bond] current width: " .. tostring(bond.ui.WIDTH) .. "<reset>\n") return end bond.ui.WIDTH = math.floor(w) -- Rebuild from scratch so the bar + tiles re-anchor to the new width, and -- the banner follows. bond.ui.reset() cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Buff bar width set to <yellow>" .. bond.ui.WIDTH .. "<reset> px.\n") end
function bond.ui.hide() bond.ui.forced = "off" pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:hide() end) if bond.ui.slots then for _, t in pairs(bond.ui.slots) do pcall(function() t:hide() end) end end if bond.ui.stopTicker then bond.ui.stopTicker() end -- Give the banner its full width back so hiding the bar doesn't leave a gap. if bond.ui.fitBanner then bond.ui.fitBanner(true) end end
-- Recompute position (after a resolution change or if icesus.core loads late). function bond.ui.reset() pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:hide() end) bond.ui.panel = nil bond.ui.slots = nil bond.ui.container = nil bond.ui.forced = "on" local ok, err = pcall(function() bond.ui.ensure() end) if not ok then cecho("\n<red>[bond] buff panel failed to build:<reset> " .. tostring(err) .. "\n") cecho("<grey>[bond] type 'buffbar where' to see which step failed.<reset>\n") return end pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:show() end) pcall(function() bond.ui.panel:raise() end) if next(bond.buffs) then bond.ui.rebuild() end send("templar_command list all") cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Buff bar re-anchored and shown.\n") end
-- Diagnostic: report the bar's computed geometry and state. function bond.ui.where() local x, y, w, h = bond.ui.geometry() cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Buff bar diagnostics:\n") cecho(string.format(" computed anchor : x=%s y=%s w=%s h=%s\n", tostring(x), tostring(y), tostring(w), tostring(h))) cecho(" intent (forced) : <yellow>" .. tostring(bond.ui.forced or "auto") .. "<reset>\n") cecho(" bar exists : " .. tostring(bond.ui.panel ~= nil) .. "\n") local nb = 0 ; for _ in pairs(bond.buffs) do nb = nb + 1 end cecho(" tracked buffs : <yellow>" .. nb .. "<reset>\n") local R = icesus and icesus.hud and icesus.hud.right cecho(" right column : " .. (R and "found (anchoring to it)" or "not found (using fallback)") .. "\n") if bond.ui.diag and #bond.ui.diag > 0 then cecho(" build trace:\n") for _, line in ipairs(bond.ui.diag) do local col = line:find("ERR") and "red" or "grey" cecho(" <" .. col .. ">" .. line .. "<reset>\n") end end if nb == 0 then cecho(" <grey>tip: run 'tcla' to populate, or cast a buff. With intent=on the empty bar still shows.<reset>\n") end end
-- Hook UI refresh into the data-change points (functions defined earlier). do -- `list all` arrives as a burst of lines; debounce to one rebuild per burst. local _parse = bond.parseSpellLine bond.parseSpellLine = function(elem, rest) _parse(elem, rest) if bond.ui._debounce then killTimer(bond.ui._debounce) end bond.ui._debounce = tempTimer(0.2, function() bond.ui._debounce = nil bond.ui.rebuild() end) end
local _clear = bond.clearBuffs bond.clearBuffs = function() _clear(); bond.ui.rebuild() end
local _ended = bond.endedSpell bond.endedSpell = function(name) _ended(name); bond.ui.rebuild() end
local _endedAll = bond.endedAll bond.endedAll = function() _endedAll(); bond.ui.rebuild() end end
cecho("\n<cyan>[bond]<reset> Templar Elemental Bond Manager v2.9.16 (always-on styled panel, build corner-8) loaded. Type <yellow>bondhelp<reset> for commands.\n") cecho("<grey>[bond]<reset> Type <yellow>buffbar<reset> to show the buff panel, or run <yellow>tcla<reset> to populate it.\n")
-- If the bar is set to always-on (the default), build and show it now so the -- styled panel appears immediately -- no need to type `buffbar`. Deferred a -- tick so icesus.core's HUD (which we anchor to) is fully constructed first. if bond.ui.forced == "on" then tempTimer(0.5, function() pcall(function() bond.ui.ensure() end) pcall(function() bond.ui.rebuild() end) -- Ask the game for current buffs so the bar fills in right away. if isConnected and isConnected() then send(bond.cmd .. " list all") end end) end
